questions.title: Linear Search Index
questions.description:
Search an unsorted vector for the first position holding the target value. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int linear_search(const std::vector<int> &v, int target)

It must return the smallest index i with v[i] == target, or -1 when the target does not appear.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000

questions.title: Binary Search on Sorted Data
questions.description:
The vector is sorted strictly ascending with distinct values. Locate the target with binary search — halve the candidate range on every step. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int binary_search_idx(const std::vector<int> &v, int target)

It must return the index holding target, or -1 when it is absent.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (strictly ascending). Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, values strictly increasing, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10000, values strictly increasing, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000

questions.title: Count Occurrences in Sorted Data
questions.description:
The vector is sorted ascending and may contain duplicates. Count how many times the target appears. Combine a left-biased and a right-biased binary search: count = last - first + 1. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_occurrences(const std::vector<int> &v, int target)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (sorted ascending). Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the number of occurrences.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, values sorted ascending, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000

questions.title: Is the Search Input Sorted
questions.description:
Binary search only works on sorted input. Write the checker that validates that precondition: report whether the vector is non-decreasing. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_sorted_vec(const std::vector<int> &v)

It must return true when every element is <= the next one. The harness prints 1 for true and 0 for false.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 if the vector is sorted ascending, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: First Defective Sensor Reading
questions.description:
A sensor loop streams calibration readings; any NEGATIVE reading marks a defective sensor. Scan the stream left to right and report the 1-based position of the first defective reading. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int first_defective(const std::vector<int> &v)

It must return the 1-based index of the first negative value, or -1 when every reading is non-negative.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated readings.

Output Format:
One line with the 1-based position, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -1000000 <= readings <= 1000000

questions.title: Employee ID Lookup

questions.title: Hottest Day Position
questions.description:
A weather station logged one temperature per day. A linear sweep is the most efficient way to find the peak when the data is unsorted. Report the 0-based index of the hottest day — on ties use the EARLIEST such day. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int hottest_day(const std::vector<int> &t)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated temperatures.

Output Format:
One line with the 0-based index of the maximum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, -60 <= temperatures <= 60

questions.title: Manual Lower-Bound Index
questions.description:
A telemetry archive is sorted ascending. Queries ask for the first slot whose value is >= the query (the "lower bound" position): the smallest index i with v[i] >= target, or n when every element is smaller. Implement it as a manual binary search — std::lower_bound is banned on this device. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int first_ge(const std::vector<int> &v, int target)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers (sorted ascending). Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the smallest index i such that v[i] >= target, or n if no such index exists.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, values sorted ascending, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10000, values sorted ascending, -1000000 <= values, target <= 1000000

questions.title: Integer Root by Binary Search
questions.description:
A firmware module must compute the integer square root of n: the largest integer r with r * r <= n. It has no floating-point unit, so binary-search the answer over [1, 1000000000]. No sqrt, no pow. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long floor_root(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the largest r such that r * r <= n.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000000000000

questions.title: First Faulty Machine in the Row
questions.description:
A production row was audited: machines report 0 (ok) or 1 (faulty) and the audit walk was done left to right, so the report is a sorted array of 0s followed by 1s. Find the index of the FIRST faulty machine with a binary search — calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int first_faulty(const std::vector<int> &v)

It must return the first index holding 1, or -1 when every machine is ok.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n entries (0 or 1, sorted ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the first index of 1, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, entries are 0 or 1, sorted ascending
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 10000, entries are 0 or 1, sorted ascending

    int rotated_search(const std::vector<int> &v, int target)

questions.title: Minimum Ship Capacity
questions.description:
A freight scheduler must move packages in the given order within a fixed number of days: each day it loads packages left to right until adding the next one would exceed the day's capacity. Find the MINIMUM capacity that finishes within the allowed days. Binary-search the answer between the heaviest package and the total weight. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long min_capacity(const std::vector<int> &w, int days)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated package weights (in shipping order). Line 3: days.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum capacity.

Constraints:
1 <= days <= n <= 1000, 1 <= weights <= 1000
